fields.System.Title: INV-3 — Moving stock
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

The single write path that every other module calls when stock needs to change hands. If this
is correct, the system is honest. If it is not, nothing built on it can be trusted.

Scope

In. Moving stock between locations, destination validation, negative stock prevention, row
locking under concurrency.

Out. Deciding why stock should move. Inbound, outbound, counting, and replenishment
decide that; this feature executes and records.

Design notes

Three defences against lost updates, used together.

1. Write deltas, not computed values. "Add minus eight", never "set to two". The database
serialises the arithmetic.
2. Lock the row when you must read before writing (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE).
3. Sort location IDs before locking, so two transactions touching A and B never deadlock.

Reject, do not clamp. A move that would take stock negative fails loudly. Clamping to zero
produces a balance that looks fine and hides the bug that caused it.

Every move writes a movement, in the same transaction, always. No exceptions, no
convenience paths, no test helpers that skip it.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Lost update on concurrent moves | [doc 09 §4.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Deadlock from inconsistent lock ordering | [doc 09 §4.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Balance changed without a movement | [doc 09 §2.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Lock contention on a popular product | [doc 09 §4.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Move into a blocked or illegal location | [doc 05 WF 3](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
